title: Request mismatch map and probe notes (2026-10-12)
content:
Context:
This is an intermediate synthesis from CS field notes (Aug–Oct 2026) capturing a set of related customer asks that we are calling the "request mismatch" cluster. These are recurring asks where customers want predictable inference behavior (latency/cost/reliability) but surface-level asks vary: retries, model fallback, per-route performance guarantees, and clearer guidance on batching/quantization tradeoffs.

Purpose:
- Create a single map of distinct customer-visible problems that are probably the same underlying gaps in documentation, runtime defaults, and rollout UX.
- Propose lightweight probes (low-effort experiments) we can run with customers to validate impact and preferred fixes.

Representative customer notes (verbatim fragments):
- "One minute cold-starts during spikes — we back off to CPU-serving and results are unpredictable" (fintech customer)
- "We tried autoscale; throughput dropped 30% when requests used functions — seems like routing changed models" (marketplace app)
- "Embeddings latency varies across regions; sometimes Dedicated rosters appear to serve older model revs" (research platform)

Observed symptom buckets (map):
1) Latency spikes tied to mixed workload routing
   - Customers see tail latency increase when small synchronous chat calls interleave with large-batch embeddings jobs.
   - Possible root: smart-routing decisions favor cost-tier routing that shifts some requests to lower-tier instances during load.

2) Model version drift during rollouts
   - Reports of requests served by older model variants after a canary rollout.
   - Possible root: cache/KV shards not invalidated or routing table stale across dedicated pools.

3) Retry and error surface confusion
   - Customers retry when errors appear, which amplifies load and worsens SLO breaches. They ask for clearer retry guidance and circuit-breaker controls.

4) Batching and quantization guidance gap
   - Teams uncertain when to enable aggressive batching/quantization because they fear quality regressions in prod.

Priority request list (clustered & reworded):
- Per-route latency SLA guidance and simple per-route toggles for "prefer-low-latency" vs "prefer-cost" (customer-facing toggle).
- Explicit model-rollout consistency check and a small UX to force a progressive cache invalidation during canaries.
- Retry/circuit-breaker defaults that are safe for mixed workloads; a sample policy for chat + embeddings mixed traffic.
- A short decision matrix doc: "Batching/Quantization: when to apply each (examples + thresholds)".

Impact hypothesis (for prioritization):
- Fixing routing + rollout visibility => reduces customer escalations by ~40% for affected accounts (from CS anecdote).
- Providing clear retry/cb policy => reduces self-amplifying spikes and lowers token-cost variance during incidents.

Proposed probes (quick experiments):
A) Per-route toggle pilot (2 weeks)
   - Pick 3 customers (one fintech, one marketplace, one enterprise search) to enable a new header "x-redwood-prefer-latency: true". Measure tail-p99 latency, token cost, and error rate vs baseline.
   - Outcome signal: p99 delta, customer qualitative feedback.

B) Canary cache-invalidation experiment (1 week)
   - Instrument rollout path to explicitly send cache-invalidation messages to Dedicated pools during canary->100% transition for a small model. Track %requests served by new rev after step.
   - Outcome: % of requests on new model within timing window.

C) Retry policy template (ongoing)
   - Ship a short sample policy in CS playbook and ask 10 pilot customers to adopt. Collect telemetry on retry counts, incident frequency.

Open questions / unknowns to resolve before broader work:
- Are there existing routing metrics we can expose per-tenant that show decision triggers? (ask platform-engineering)
- Do Dedicated pools already have a per-pool cache invalidation API we can safely call during rollouts? (ask serving-runtime)
- What are constraints for adding a header-based toggle on hosted API without widening attack surface? (security)

Stakeholders and immediate owners:
- Probe A owner: product-hosted-api (Priya Raman to lead, CS supporting)
- Probe B owner: serving-runtime (Ethan Kim to coordinate with infra)
- Retry policy doc: customer-success + SRE (Marisol Ortega + Diego Alvarez)

Proposed timeline & next steps (next 6 weeks):
- Week 0: Review draft with Platform and Serving leads (this doc + quick sync).
- Week 1–2: Build Pilot flags + basic telemetry dashboards (small infra changes).
- Week 3: Onboard 3 pilot customers for toggle; run 14-day measurement.
- Week 4–6: Iterate on retry policy and prepare a public CS note with example configs.

Quick wins (low-effort items we can ship in ~1 sprint):
- CS playbook snippet: recommended retry backoff parameters for mixed chat+embed workloads.
- Short FAQ on what to expect during canaries and how to surface model-version mismatches to support (Slack tag + sample cURL to capture headers).

Risks and mitigation:
- Pilot flag could change billing dynamics for customers unintentionally — add an opt-in consent step and billing monitoring.
- Cache invalidation at scale could cause transient errors — limit to small model and slow ramp for first runs.

Appendix: sample telemetry queries (quick notes)
- p99_latency_by_route = query(trace_table, filter=route, agg=p99(duration))
- model_rev_staleness = fraction(events where response.model_rev != deployed_target_rev)

Notes to self / CS shorthand (untidy):
- Several customers equivocate "slow" vs "inconsistent"; emphasize "tail variance" in probes.
- Link to ext: see Confluence-54321 for prior canary notes.
- TODO: attach Slack thread r/infra for cache invalidation (Priya to paste link).

If you want to run through a condensed slide for Exec next Monday, I can draft a 3-slide pitch (Problem map + pilot plan + ask).

— Marisol
